Build me a dense central-Paris-style urban district with a quiet, slightly overcast atmosphere, formed by roughly twenty tightly packed mid-rise perimeter blocks arranged along a network of narrow streets and a few wider intersecting avenues. Use irregular trapezoidal, triangular, and polygonal blocks that follow angled roads, with nearly continuous street-facing façades and enclosed interior courtyards; several courtyards should remain visibly unfinished, with tall plain off-white inner walls and flat gray paving. Make the buildings predominantly six to seven stories tall in a consistent Haussmannian style: pale weathered stone façades, repetitive tall windows, black wrought-iron balcony rails, dark gray mansard roofs, dormer windows, chimneys, decorative cornices, and occasional arched blue or red doors. Cluster the blocks closely enough to create urban canyons, while allowing chamfered corners and wedge-shaped buildings to define junctions. Cover the ground with dark asphalt roads, broad gray stone sidewalks, painted lane arrows, dashed markings, zebra crossings, and small traffic islands. Place black bollards and metal pedestrian railings along selected curbs, traffic lights at a prominent intersection, a red no-entry sign on a side street, and scattered street signs and poles. Add a bicycle rack with several bicycles beside a corner bistro, sparse young sidewalk trees, a few benches or café chairs, and occasional small street clutter, but almost no people or vehicles. Keep the terrain flat and terminate the outer edges with abruptly cut building blocks, blank courtyard shells, gray ground planes, and an empty pale sky.

=== THE TASK ===
Rebuild the place described above on the 200 m x 200 m plate, at the density
and arrangement the description calls for. Budget is 800 tool calls and 180

clauses.text: Build me a dense central-Paris-style urban district with a quiet, slightly overcast atmosphere, formed by roughly twenty tightly packed mid-rise perimeter blocks arranged along a network of narrow streets and a few wider intersecting avenues
Use irregular trapezoidal, triangular, and polygonal blocks that follow angled roads, with nearly continuous street-facing façades and enclosed interior courtyards
several courtyards should remain visibly unfinished, with tall plain off-white inner walls and flat gray paving

Make the buildings predominantly six to seven stories tall in a consistent Haussmannian style: pale weathered stone façades, repetitive tall windows, black wrought-iron balcony rails, dark gray mansard roofs, dormer windows, chimneys, decorative cornices, and occasional arched blue or red doors
Cluster the blocks closely enough to create urban canyons, while allowing chamfered corners and wedge-shaped buildings to define junctions
Cover the ground with dark asphalt roads, broad gray stone sidewalks, painted lane arrows, dashed markings, zebra crossings, and small traffic islands
Place black bollards and metal pedestrian railings along selected curbs, traffic lights at a prominent intersection, a red no-entry sign on a side street, and scattered street signs and poles
Add a bicycle rack with several bicycles beside a corner bistro, sparse young sidewalk trees, a few benches or café chairs, and occasional small street clutter, but almost no people or vehicles
Keep the terrain flat and terminate the outer edges with abruptly cut building blocks, blank courtyard shells, gray ground planes, and an empty pale sky
